name: pigeon-84677d84-blind29-ots
instr:
# pigeon-regen

This is a command line tool that takes a description of a language's syntax and writes out source code for a reader of that language. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the accepted notation changed and no caller changed, yet descriptions that were handled correctly before are now handled wrongly, and many that used to be accepted are refused outright.

Trouble begins the moment the tool is run from a terminal. Naming a description file as the single non-flag argument no longer reads that file: the name is ignored and the text is taken from the stream piped in instead, while invoking the tool with no argument at all, which should read the piped stream, fails complaining that it cannot open something. The status the process finally exits with no longer agrees with what happened during the run, so a help request, a run that found nothing to work on, and a rejected pair of file arguments can no longer be told apart from outside.

Hand it a description and text that is entirely ordinary now draws complaints, or comes back chopped up in ways that do not match the source. The lowercase a is no longer counted among the characters a name may be built from, so any name holding it is split in two there, while names built from other lowercase characters, or from capitals, come through whole. No decimal numeral counts either, so a name with one inside it splits at that point too. Inside a string literal, an escape written as a backsl
